source: Now you know the truth. I hope it brings you boundless happiness.
Why won't you talk to me, Brit? Is something that horribly wrong?
I could, if you'd tell me.
I'm sure by now you've heard the rumors about a Norwegian confidante within Elsinore's court.
You're not saying... the spy... is...
Yes. Well, really, it's my father, but he gets his information from me.
My father is angry with Claudius. He's been trying to centralize power behind the throne.
He finds him unfit to rule, and believes Claudius misled the nobility about his intentions when they elected him King.
But if Claudius is murdered, everyone will suspect my father was behind it.
So my father plotted a secret coup.
A rebellion from within Elsinore's walls. Coax a man who already dislikes Claudius into offing him.
That man is your brother.
Laertes? But Laertes wouldn't attack the throne of Denmark. He's frustrated, certainly, but he's not a natural killer.
...He would be if you were dead. Everyone sees the love your brother has for you. It's unparalleled.
I don't know why I'm telling you this.
Maybe because you were the only one who'd ever been kind to me in this horrid place.
And whatever little it means, I'm sorry for this. I didn't want to do this. I really didn't.
You can still choose not to.
No. I can't.
Perished at Brit's hand.

source: If Fortinbras's invasion were rebuked, your father would have no choice but to work with the king.
And that might grant a more lasting peace than anything Claudius's death could provide.
But that's impossible. How are you going to repel a national invasion?
I don't know. But there's got to be a way.
I wouldn't have told you this before, but—Fortinbras is already here. Just outside Elsinore. He's been here a little over a week.
I've been visiting him. In town. He's staying in a small room with some officers, in civilian dress.
They meet late at night in the town square, long after all are asleep. They plan to meet next right before the siege begins on Sunday.
I can get you into that meeting. But you... can't reveal me. You have to pretend to be loyal to Norway, no matter what you see or hear.
Understood. I won't expose you, Brit. I swear it.
If you're lying to me...
I'm not.
Be there. I'll take care of the rest.
I know.
What? How--
It's a long story. But I know.
I'm convinced you're some kind of witch. Just haven't figured out if you're using your powers for good or evil.
In this case, it's for your good. Trust me on that.
Well, if you want to meet the Prince, he and I have a standing rendezvous.
But you... can't reveal me. You have to pretend to be loyal to Norway, no matter what you see or hear.
It'll end poorly for both of us if I'm there. I'd rather not.
You sound strange.
Call it a hunch of sorts.
Well, come to the meeting or don't. I'll be safe regardless. Blue blood is just as blue no matter who wears our country's crown.
Ophelia. A word in private, please?
It's nothing. I merely came to... thank you.
Claudius is dead. And Hamlet and I will be betrothed soon.
Claudius is dead. I'm hearing rumors that Hamlet and I are to be betrothed soon.
I thought you'd be happier, somehow.
That makes two of us.
This may be only a temporary arrangement. If Fortinbras arrives, I'm certain our betrothal will be disbanded as soon as possible.
And then, under his rule, I will become Fortinbras' wife. The Queen of Denmark.
But in either case, with either of these men, I should be overjoyed. I'm out of my father's hands now. He can't control me from the throne of Denmark.
I can paint any time I like. I can paint the whole castle if I so desire.
At first I thought this meant I was free—more free than I've ever been in my life.
But I'm not really. My ownership has merely changed hands.
I'm sorry, Brit. I wanted this to be good for you.
(Perhaps if Hamlet were betrothed already... no. That's a thought I ought not to explore.)
(I wonder if there's a world where Brit wouldn't have to be wed.)
Don't apologize. You've done everything I asked. And you've showed me kindness.
The invasion comes for us all soon enough, but when the dust has settled, I know at least that you and I will be all right.
With Claudius dead, Fortinbras has assured my father that Elsinore will fall all the more swiftly.
He will liberate the castle tomorrow and formally place it under Norwegian rule.
And now, at last, I am free.
Certainly. With Hamlet gone, there's no suitable betrothal left to make within this family line.
I will allow Gertrude to remain here, given all she's done for me, of course.
Certainly. Hamlet is betrothed—to you, in fact—preventing anyone from trying to barter a truce.
If not for that, we'd be halfway to the altar by now. You've saved me from such a fate.
Provided Hamlet doesn't stand in Fortinbras' way, the future before us is a painless one.
Now I can sit the throne of Elsinore in peace. Until the nobility can sort out which poor sod of a man gets to marry me, that is.
The throne?
Yes. I am to be crowned Queen regnant, as soon as the nobles are able to congregate.
I have their unanimous approval, thanks to my father's lobbying.
I didn't know. You'll make for a fearsome queen, Brit.
Thanks. Speaking of which...
Ophelia. Er. I-- well.
This is hard to say.
I'm sorry. I was needlessly cruel to you. For years, in fact.
But you were kind to me, again and again, regardless.
You made me feel like I had choice again. As though my life were not as ironclad as I had imagined.
I hope things can be different between us. I hope we can be something else.
Are we friends?
Oh, no, no. I haven't got any friends, and I plan to keep it that way. But 'allies' may be sufficient.
I'll take it.
Brit asked me to meet her in town around this time.
Go to Castle Town?

source: I won't go yet, though.
Naturally, I've arrived early.
So you did come after all.
Go to the Fortinbras Meeting?

source: Ophelia? What are you doing here?
Ophelia? What are you doing out here?
You can see me?
No, I'm clearly talking to the wall.
Yes, I can see you. This area's rather well-lit.
I was taking an evening stroll.
What about yourself?
Well, I was having a nice personal break from my mountain of courtly duties.
Until you came along. Stop following me.
She practically ran from me.
I suppose this area is a lot better lit than the docks. That tactic won't work here.
Stay silent. Say nothing. If asked, reply only 'yes, my lord,' or 'no, my lord.' That is all. Do you understand?
Come on, then. I hear their boots nearby.
Ah, Brit... I've had a change of heart.
Meeting Fortinbras would end poorly for me. Trust me, I know it.
After all that, huh?
Well. I guess I'm on my own. Even now.
I know about everything, Brit. I know you've been leaking information to Norway. I know about your family. Your father. Fortinbras.
All I want is to hear what Fortinbras has to say. I know he'll meet with you tonight. I want to be present.
You? Present for this?
(I hear their boots... they're coming now...)
Fine. You must be some kind of witch, but you've always been obsessed with me, so I ought to have known it'd come to this.
Come on, then.
Good evening, my lord.
Lady Birgitta. Tomorrow is the morning we've waited for.
All attempts at a coup have failed. No other bloodless option remains.
...Who is this?
My servant, Your Majesty. She speaks little Danish, and she's quite the ignorant clout.
Can she be trusted?
As I was saying, we must attack head on. We will begin by sieging the town at dawn.
Are you prepared to assist us in getting into the castle by any means necessary?
...There is no need, my lord. The King is already preoccupied.
You will be able to enter with ease. The castle will be ill prepared.
Excellent. I so detest needless bloodshed.
It is my uncle's way to murder and poison his way to the top. Not mine.
Mind you be clear of this town at dawn. My men have already begun their approach.
I wish no harm to come to any Danes. But if they protest, then I shall lay down my boot unflinchingly.
Still, I have high hopes to take Prince Hamlet alive. From what his subjects say, I believe him to be a good man at heart.
And you will be his bride.
Are you not eager? This is a great honor for your family.
I am. It's just... he's been through so much lately. I fear he'll be broken by the time this siege is over.
He seems odd and mad lately. Not in his right mind. Please... have your men be gentle with him.
I will. We'll take him prisoner as quickly as possible. He'll be surrounded by all members of his family who submit to the authority of Norway.
Hamlet has passed away, in truth. He'll never be King now.
I see. I hadn't heard the news. Now cracks a noble heart.
My younger brother, then. Or someone of his like. We shall see who yet has the muster to rule this country fittingly.
Mind you be clear of this town at dawn, my lady.
...One last, unfortunate thing.
Your servant girl here.
I once heard the most fascinating story about the Danish court.
They say that a woman of some noble birth with a dark look about her held the Danish Prince's heart.
And you, Lady Brit, mentioned yourself that a certain young girl's death could bring about Claudius's demise at her brother's hand.
The way she stands, the way she looks... this woman is no clout, nor is she common.
It's true. I am Lady Ophelia.
Given your desire to overtake my country, I cannot rightly say it is a pleasure to make your acquaintance, Prince Fortinbras.
I assume you're going to kill me now.
Unfortunately, you're correct. I cannot let you return to Elsinore and warn the others. A full defense mounted against us would mean more death.
Although I truly despise the killing of women, in this case, we have no sufficient place in which to hold you until our work is complete.
I shall need every man available for our coup, and this town may well be rubble if the castle will not surrender.
It is a most regrettable situation.
My lord, please... y-you're really going to kill her?
B-but she was just—she hasn't—done anything wrong!
I was the one who brought her—
Quiet, Brit.
My lord, if you're going to kill me anyway, then please, tell me...
